name: Lin Zhenhua
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Sichuan Kexin Mechanical and Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300092)
profile: Lin Zhenhua (林祯华) chairs Sichuan Kexin Mechanical & Electrical, a Shenzhen-listed maker of large heavy-duty pressure vessels and process equipment for nuclear power, new energy, petrochemical and coal/gas chemical plants. He is its largest individual shareholder (~15.6%), with Lin Zhenrong holding a similar stake; re-elected to the board in 2020.
interesting_fact: Kexin's heavy pressure vessels are supplied into nuclear power and new-energy projects, putting a Sichuan family-run equipment maker in the energy-infrastructure supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MBA from Sichuan University and has also been a director of Sichuan Sunshine Plastics since 2007.
notes: Very low public profile; no English bio. Best route is likely the company's board secretary (董秘) contact listed in Kexin's annual report on cninfo.com.cn; company website could not be loaded. Wealth shared with Lin Zhenfu / Lin Zhenrong.

name: Ajit S Shriram
current_role: Joint Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd.
profile: Ajit S. Shriram is the youngest of three brothers (with Ajay and Vikram Shriram) running DCM Shriram, the Delhi-based conglomerate spun out of the old DCM Group in 1990, spanning chlor-alkali chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, Bioseed, Fenesta windows and PVC. He has served on the board for about two decades.
interesting_fact: He is a past President of the Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) and a member of the CII National Council on Agriculture.
deep_cut_fact: After a commerce degree from Osmania University, Hyderabad, he did his MBA at IMD Lausanne; his company bio lists his passions as travel, photography and theatre.
notes: Press email is the published Corporate Communication/CSR contact (Ms. Aman Pannu). Energy angle: DCM Shriram is a large captive power and chlor-alkali (energy-intensive) operator.

name: Aroon Purie
current_role: Chairman & Editor-in-Chief, India Today Group; Chairman & MD, TV Today Network
profile: Aroon Purie (b. 1944) is the founder-publisher and editor-in-chief of India Today, launched in 1975, and built the India Today Group into a diversified media house (Aaj Tak, India Today TV, magazines, radio, printing via Thomson Press). In 2017 he passed day-to-day control to daughter Kalli Purie but remains editor-in-chief.
interesting_fact: Awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2001; in 2025 at FICCI Frames he warned AI poses an 'existential threat' to credible journalism.
deep_cut_fact: A chartered accountant and LSE economics graduate (1965), he began his career in 1970 as a production controller at the family's Thomson Press printing business; he was a Doon School contemporary of Rajiv Gandhi.
notes: No published personal or press email found; route via India Today Group corporate office/editorial. Media figure rather than energy; AI-in-media views may be a hook.

name: Ming Dequan
profile: Listed (Hurun China 2006-2007) as the founder behind Celestial NutriFoods, a Chinese maker of soybean-protein foods (Sun Moon Star brand). Could not find sources confirming his role or current status.
notes: Searches found no public record linking the name to Celestial NutriFoods; company appears largely defunct/delisted. Not a viable guest without further verification.

name: Venugopal Dhoot
current_role: Former Chairman, Videocon Group (company taken over in insolvency)
profile: Venugopal Dhoot built Videocon from a colour-TV maker launched with his father Nandlal Dhoot into a consumer-durables, DTH, telecom and oil & gas conglomerate, appearing on Forbes lists 2007-2015. Videocon Industries went into insolvency and was taken over; he no longer runs an operating business.
interesting_fact: Videocon started by making colour televisions in India and grew into one of the country's best-known consumer electronics brands, later expanding into oil & gas exploration (Brazil, Mozambique stakes).
notes: Not recommended: subject of ongoing ICICI loan case (arrested Dec 2022, on bail) and personal insolvency proceedings upheld by NCLAT in 2026. No published contact route found.

name: Sankar Sen
profile: Shankar (Sankar/Shaankar) Sen, founder chairman and MD of Kolkata jeweller Senco Gold, died on 28 July 2020. His son Suvankar Sen now leads the company as MD & CEO.
notes: Deceased 28 July 2020 (source: indianjeweller.in obituary). Successor at Senco Gold: Suvankar Sen.

name: Daniel Masters
current_role: Co-founder and Non-executive Director (former Executive Chairman), CoinShares
profile: Daniel Masters (b. 1963) is a veteran energy trader turned crypto pioneer. After heading global energy trading at Morgan Guaranty Trust and working in Salomon's energy division, he founded Jersey-based commodities manager Global Advisors, launched the world's first regulated bitcoin fund (GABI) in 2014, and co-founded CoinShares, now a Nasdaq-listed digital-asset manager.
interesting_fact: He launched GABI, described as the world's first regulated bitcoin fund, out of Jersey in 2014 - years before institutional crypto ETPs.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he helped establish the UK's natural gas and electricity markets, completed some of the first forward contracts for electricity, and was among the earliest active traders in European Contracts for Difference.
notes: Excellent energy+crypto fit: physics graduate (Exeter), MSc OR (Imperial), 30+ years in energy trading. Route via CoinShares press office.

name: Stephen Trundle
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Alarm.com Holdings (Nasdaq: ALRM)
profile: Steve Trundle has run Alarm.com since 2003, after serving as a technology executive (CTO) at MicroStrategy, where Alarm.com began as an R&D spinoff in 2000. He led it through a 2009 management buyout and a 2015 IPO; it is now a large cloud platform for connected security, video and smart-home/energy management.
interesting_fact: Alarm.com bought demand-response/DERMS firm EnergyHub in 2013, now a grid-flexibility platform for utilities - a direct link to the energy/grid theme.
deep_cut_fact: Alarm.com was one of dozens of premium domains Michael Saylor bought for ~$2M at MicroStrategy; at the 2009 buyout ($27.7M) Trundle's company had about 150,000 customers sold through ~800 dealers. Trundle holds a Dartmouth degree in engineering sciences and government.
notes: Press email = Alarm.com Public Relations contact named on 2025 releases; IR = Investor and Media Relations contact (2025). Verify current names on latest Business Wire release.

name: Jaya Bachchan
current_role: Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha (Samajwadi Party, Uttar Pradesh), serving since 2004
profile: Jaya Bachchan (née Bhaduri, b. 1948) is a celebrated Hindi film actress (ten Filmfare Awards, Padma Shri) and a Samajwadi Party Rajya Sabha MP since 2004. Her listed wealth is held jointly with husband Amitabh Bachchan, largely via investments and film/real-estate assets.
interesting_fact: She made her screen debut at 14 in Satyajit Ray's Bengali film Mahanagar (1963), and her first adult lead was Hrishikesh Mukherjee's Guddi (1971).
deep_cut_fact: Inspired by working with Satyajit Ray, she enrolled at the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, and graduated with a gold medal.
notes: Office email is her official Rajya Sabha (sansad.nic.in) address as carried in OpenSanctions' copy of the Rajya Sabha member dataset; verify on sansad.in. Known to be media-averse; poor fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Mark L Baum
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Harrow, Inc. (Nasdaq: HROW)
profile: Mark L. Baum founded Harrow (formerly Imprimis Pharmaceuticals) in 2011-12 and built it into a leading North American eye-care pharmaceutical company. A lawyer by training, he previously ran private investment fund TBLF, making 200+ investments in 40+ companies, and co-founded Eton Pharmaceuticals, Melt Pharmaceuticals and Surface Ophthalmics.
interesting_fact: Named EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2017 (life sciences, San Diego); an outspoken advocate on drug pricing with WSJ op-eds and appearances on CNN, CBS, Bloomberg and others.
deep_cut_fact: In 1999 - well before Harrow - he founded YesRx, an HIV-focused pharmacy business. He graduated cum laude from UT Arlington and from California Western School of Law in 1997.
notes: IR email belongs to Mike Biega, VP Investor Relations & Communications, listed as investor & media contact on 2026 releases. Media-friendly CEO; pharma rather than energy.

name: Alexis P Michas
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Juniper Investment Company; Non-Executive Chair of Revvity and of BorgWarner
profile: Alexis P. Michas is a Harvard College/HBS-educated private-equity investor who founded Juniper Investment Company in 2008. He chairs the boards of Revvity (formerly PerkinElmer, on its board since 2001) and auto/e-mobility supplier BorgWarner, sits on Cenergy Holdings' board, and holds a 10%+ stake in Orthofix.
interesting_fact: He chairs BorgWarner, a major supplier pivoting to EV propulsion, and sits on the board of Cenergy Holdings, the Greek maker of power cables and steel pipes for energy grids and offshore wind.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the U.S. Board of Trustees of Athens College in Greece.
notes: Low public profile investor; no published personal/firm email found. Energy angle via Cenergy (cables for grid/offshore wind) and BorgWarner. Route via Juniper Investment Company or company corporate secretaries.

name: Shelley Simpson
current_role: President & CEO, J.B. Hunt Transport Services (since July 2024)
profile: Shelley Simpson joined J.B. Hunt in 1994 as an hourly customer service rep straight out of the University of Arkansas and rose through the ranks - creating its Integrated Capacity Solutions brokerage unit, becoming chief commercial officer (2017) and president (2022) - before succeeding John Roberts as CEO of the Fortune 500 freight carrier in 2024.
interesting_fact: She is one of the few Fortune 500 CEOs to have started at the company in an entry-level hourly job, climbing from customer service to CEO over 30 years.
deep_cut_fact: A Russellville, Arkansas native, she launched J.B. Hunt's ICS brokerage unit in 2007 with 18 employees; by 2014 it had 540 people and $535M+ revenue.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearance: Walton College 'Be EPIC' podcast ep. 189

notes: Press contact is Brittnee Davie, VP Marketing, via press@jbhunt.com. Has done podcasts before (Be EPIC, FreightWaves events) - receptive to media.

name: Richard Deal
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Human Resources Officer, FICO (Fair Isaac Corp.)
profile: Richard S. 'Rich' Deal is FICO's long-serving HR chief: he joined in 2001 as VP of Human Resources, became SVP & CHRO in 2007 and EVP & CHRO in 2015. His wealth stems from FICO equity accumulated as the analytics/credit-scoring company's share price soared. Earlier he held HR roles at Arcadia Financial and U.S. Bancorp.
interesting_fact: He has spent roughly 25 years at FICO, leading talent strategy and acquisition-integration work through its transformation into a high-margin scores and decisioning-software business.
deep_cut_fact: Before FICO he was VP of Human Resources at Arcadia Financial (1998-2001) and held HR consulting and line roles at U.S. Bancorp (1993-1998).
notes: Low public profile HR executive; limited relevance for energy/data-center themes. Route via FICO media relations.

name: Steven J Hilton
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Meritage Homes (NYSE: MTH)
profile: Steve Hilton (b. 1961) co-founded Scottsdale homebuilder Monterey Homes in 1985 at age 24; it became Meritage Homes in 1997. As CEO until 2021 he grew it from under 300 homes a year to a top-10 US builder delivering 130,000+ homes, and he remains Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: He led Meritage's 2011 'Green Program' of energy-efficient homes, making it a multi-year US DOE Energy Star Partner of the Year; Builder named him CEO of the Year in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: He has held a minority ownership stake in the NBA's Phoenix Suns since 2004, and was named an Entrepreneurial Fellow by the University of Arizona's Eller College (his alma mater, accounting & finance '83) in 2006.
notes: Contact person on both addresses: Emily Tadano, VP Investor Relations & External Communications. Good energy-efficiency angle (Energy Star homebuilding).

name: Andrew M Saperstein
current_role: Co-President, Morgan Stanley; Head of Wealth Management
profile: Andy Saperstein is co-president of Morgan Stanley and runs its wealth management business, the firm's largest, after joining in 2006 as COO of National Sales. A Wharton (summa) and Harvard Law ('93) graduate, he spent eight years at McKinsey specialising in wealth management and also worked at Merrill Lynch before Morgan Stanley.
interesting_fact: He was seen as a contender in the Morgan Stanley CEO succession race won by Ted Pick in 2023; he has been co-president since 2021.
deep_cut_fact: He left law for McKinsey after attending a recruiting presentation 'because I heard that they were serving shrimp cocktail'; his HLS roommate recalls he was an even better bowler than he was a student.
notes: Also a Teen Cancer America and Child Mind Institute supporter (bio pages on both). Route via Morgan Stanley media relations.

name: Joseph Devivo
current_role: President, CEO & Chairman, Butterfly Network (NYSE: BFLY)
profile: Joe DeVivo is a ~37-year medtech veteran who became CEO and chairman of Butterfly Network, maker of semiconductor-based handheld ultrasound, in April 2023. He previously ran InTouch Health (telehealth robots), sold to Teladoc for about $1.1B, led AngioDynamics and RITA Medical, and chaired Caption Health before its sale to GE Healthcare.
interesting_fact: Butterfly's ultrasound puts the imaging transducer on a semiconductor chip ('ultrasound-on-chip'), letting a whole-body scanner plug into a smartphone.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career he held executive roles at surgical-robotics pioneer Computer Motion and at U.S. Surgical; he is a 1989 business graduate of the University of Richmond's Robins School.
notes: Media contact: Liz Snyder, Director Communications & PR. Semiconductor/AI-imaging angle could fit a tech podcast.
